headline: IRAN TRUCE LIFTS METALS: Industrial Metals Head for Best Month Since January on 60-Day US-Iran Ceasefire
snippet: Industrial metals are on track for their best monthly gain since January after the US and Iran agreed to a 60-day ceasefire extension that launches formal nuclear talks. Copper and base metals had surrendered 2026 gains through March and April as the Iran war stoked energy-price inflation; the truce framework signals potential relief for global supply chains and manufacturing costs.

headline: TRADE SECRETS WAR: MP Materials Sues USA Rare Earth Over Magnet Tech Theft; Both Stocks Fall 3%
snippet: MP Materials filed suit in a Texas federal court alleging a former engineer shared proprietary grain-boundary-diffusion magnet formulations with USA Rare Earth, which then disclosed them to a third-party technology company. USA Rare Earth denied the claims; MP's market cap sits near $11.6B while USAR traded below $6B after the session's sell-off.

headline: GOLD AT 2-MONTH LOW: $4,501 as Fresh US-Iran Strikes Revive Inflation Trade and Delay Rate Cuts
snippet: Gold steadied near $4,501/oz — its lowest level since March — after renewed US military strikes in the Persian Gulf sent crude oil and the dollar sharply higher, reducing expectations for near-term Fed rate cuts. Gold remains up 35.7% year-over-year despite the pullback from all-time highs; Fed Governor Lisa Cook backed holding rates steady while leaving room to hike if inflation accelerates.

headline: CHINA'S SILVER BINGE: 790+ Tonnes Imported in Two Months; $77.50 Price Holds as Visible Stocks Drain
snippet: Silver held at $77.50/oz — up 2.6% on the session — as data confirmed China imported over 790 tonnes in the first two months of 2026, an eight-year high driven by solar panel and EV production. The three largest visible silver inventories across COMEX, LBMA, and Shanghai have collectively shed nearly one billion ounces since 2021, underscoring a structural supply deficit now entering its sixth consecutive year.

headline: CAMECO CLEARED: McArthur River and Key Lake Back to Full Output After Saskatchewan Flood; 2026 Guidance Intact at 19.5–21.5M lbs
snippet: Cameco confirmed both Saskatchewan flagship operations have returned to full production after the Smoothstone River Bridge partially collapsed under flood waters in early May, forcing a three-week secondary-route supply workaround. The company maintained its 2026 consolidated production guidance of 19.5–21.5 million pounds U3O8, with uranium spot holding near $86.50/lb — a two-month high — supported by nuclear power demand deals with Meta and Microsoft for AI data centres.

headline: LITHIUM COOLS 2.4%: Carbonate Slides to $25.89/kg as Australia's Bald Hill Mine Restarts After 18-Month Shutdown
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate retreated from its two-year high, falling 2.4% to $25.89/kg globally after Mineral Resources confirmed it is restarting the Bald Hill lithium mine following an 18-month suspension. Prices had doubled from roughly $13/kg in Q4 2025, driven by China's VAT rebate cut on batteries and surging energy storage demand; Morgan Stanley still forecasts an 80,000-tonne LCE deficit for 2026.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER GOES UNDERGROUND: 2,000m Phase 1 Drill Starts June 1 at Oregon Mine (TSXV: BHS)
snippet: Bayhorse Silver (TSXV: BHS) completed underground drilling preparations at its Bayhorse Silver Mine in Oregon, with the first phase 2,000-metre diamond drill program scheduled to commence June 1. The timing coincides with silver trading above $77/oz, providing strong economic incentive to confirm and expand the historic high-grade underground resource at the past-producing mine.

headline: $45M MONTANA TARGET: American Pacific Mining Fires Up 15,000m Copper-Gold Drill at Madison Project
snippet: American Pacific Mining launched a 15,000-metre drill program at its Madison Copper-Gold Project in Montana, testing a porphyry system backed by $45 million in historical exploration work that has never been fully evaluated with modern techniques. The company is targeting a maiden resource estimate on what management describes as one of the most under-drilled large-scale copper-gold targets in the western United States.

headline: NEWMONT vs. SSR MINING: Which Gold Stock to Own as Miners Finally Outpace the Metal at $4,500/oz?
snippet: With GDX up 108% year-over-year and gold miners finally showing operating leverage to record $4,500/oz gold, Motley Fool analysts pit Newmont's scale, dividend, and balance sheet discipline against SSR Mining's faster growth trajectory and acquisition-recovery story — a useful framework for retail investors deciding where to add mining equity exposure.
